title: Core: Add a manual reference-cycle collector for RefCounted
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve?

- Closes #7038

## Additional information

`RefCounted` is backed by a bare atomic reference count with no cycle
detection (`core/object/ref_counted.h`). A reference cycle — for example two
GDScript objects that hold a reference to each other, with nothing external
referencing either — never reaches zero on its own and leaks for the
lifetime of the process. The only existing guidance (documented on
`RefCounted` itself) is to manually break such cycles with `weakref()`.

**What this adds**: a `CycleCollector` (`core/object/cycle_collector.h/.cpp`)
implementing Bacon & Rajan's synchronous trial-deletion algorithm — the same
one used by CPython's `gc` module:

- On every `RefCounted::unreference()` that decrements without reaching
  zero, the object is buffered as a possible cycle root.
- The new `Engine.collect_cycles()` walks the buffered set, trial-decrementing
  a *local scratch* refcount (never the real atomic) along every reachable
  edge, and identifies as garbage anything left with a scratch count of zero
  — i.e. objects proven reachable only from within the traversed subgraph.
- Edges are only followed through a script instance's members (two new
  `ScriptInstance` virtuals — `get_gc_member_count()`/`get_gc_member()` —
  implemented by `GDScriptInstance`) and through `Array`/`Dictionary`
  contents, never through arbitrary exposed properties or getters, which
  would be unsafe to re-enter mid-collection.

**A correctness subtlety worth flagging for review**: freeing a proven cycle
isn't as simple as calling `memdelete()` on each member in turn — they still
hold live references *to each other*, so destroying one the ordinary way can
free another member as a side effect, which the collector would then try to
free again itself (double free). This is handled by padding each garbage
object's real refcount by one, severing every outgoing edge through the
ordinary safe `Variant`-release path (a third new virtual,
`clear_gc_member()`, which can't prematurely reach zero thanks to the
padding), then removing the padding with a real `unreference()` — by then
every edge within the cycle has already been severed, so this is provably
the last reference and freeing it is safe.

**Deliberate scope limits** (this is already a fairly large change; I tried
to keep it to something that could plausibly be reviewed and merged rather
than a full engine-wide GC rewrite):
- Collection is **manual only** — `Engine.collect_cycles()` must be called
  explicitly; nothing calls it automatically every frame. Whether/how to
  wire up automatic periodic collection seems like a separate design
  discussion (frequency, thread-safety implications, performance cost of
  scanning every frame vs. staleness of leaked memory).
- Must be called from the main thread. It doesn't attempt concurrent or
  incremental collection.
- Only cycles routed through GDScript members and/or `Array`/`Dictionary`
  contents are detected. A `RefCounted` with no script instance (e.g. a
  plain `Resource`) can't be the source of a detected cycle.

Given the size of this change and that #7038 has had no prior fix attempts
in ~9 years, I'd welcome input from core devs on whether this scope and API
shape (`Engine.collect_cycles()`) make sense before going further (e.g.
automatic collection, exposing it to C#/GDExtension script instances, etc.)
— happy to discuss on Contributors Chat if useful.

**Testing**: added `tests/core/object/test_cycle_collector.cpp` (3 cases: a
direct two-object cycle, a cycle routed through an `Array`, and a
false-positive check for an object referenced twice that isn't part of any
cycle — all passing). Also verified against the full existing test suite
(1423/1423 cases, 422,857/422,857 assertions, no regressions) and manually
against a real GDScript scene reproducing the original leak end-to-end.

**AI disclosure**: This change (algorithm design, implementation, and
testing) was developed with Claude (Anthropic), directed and reviewed by
me. During development, Claude's first draft of the finalization step
called `memdelete()` directly on cycle members, which it then identified
itself as unsafe (the double-free hazard described above) and corrected to
the pad/sever/release sequence before I asked for this to be verified by an
actual build and test run. I read and understand the diff before submitting
it.
